one_liner: Safe pure-Rust JPEG encoder/decoder; progressive decode 1.35x libjpeg-turbo, baseline about 6% slower single-threaded.
what_it_does: A JPEG encoder (jpegli-derived adaptive quantization, optional XYB, mozjpeg-style trellis) and decoder written in Rust with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in the crate and no C dependencies. The decoder is a Rust builder API (Decoder::new().decode(&bytes, stop), decode_into, and a row-by-row scanline_reader) with pixel and memory limits, cancellation tokens, four strictness levels, lossless DCT-domain transforms and UltraHDR gain maps. It is not a libjpeg or TurboJPEG ABI replacement and ships no C API.
how_it_is_fast: Baseline JPEGs go through a streaming single-pass decoder: Huffman decode, IDCT, chroma upsampling and YCbCr-to-RGB run per MCU row with no coefficient buffer, using fused AVX2 upsample+color-convert kernels, partial dequantization driven by the coefficient count, and a DC-only fast path. Progressive decode, the one clear single-thread win, comes from fused per-scan AC loops with a combined 9-bit Huffman+value lookup and a u64 nonzero-coefficient bitmap per block walked with trailing_zeros during AC refinement (callgrind: 415M vs 580M instructions for zune-jpeg at 2048x2048). The default IDCT is a jpegli-style integer IDCT rather than libjpeg's ISLOW, SIMD is dispatched at runtime through archmage tokens (AVX2/FMA, AVX-512, NEON, SIMD128), and with --features parallel images carrying restart markers are split by restart segment across a rayon pool.
when_to_use: Rust services that decode many progressive JPEGs (mozjpeg-style web images): 46 vs 34 MiB/s single-threaded on CID22 512x512 Q85 4:2:0, and 0.60x to 0.69x of mozjpeg's time on the Feb 2026 synthetic 256 to 4096 px set.

Latency-bound decode of large baseline JPEGs that carry restart markers (DRI) on a multi-core box, with the parallel feature: 3.05 ms vs 15.8 ms single-threaded libjpeg-turbo at 2048x2048 (multi-thread vs one thread).
Untrusted-input pipelines that want a memory-safe decoder with max_pixels/max_memory caps, cooperative cancellation and Strict to Permissive error policies.
Bounded-memory decode of very large images through the scanline reader (the wave-parallel path caps its buffer at 6 MB at 4096x4096).
Pure-Rust jpegli-quality encoding where a C++ toolchain is unwanted; the project's own note puts the encoder about 15 to 20% slower than C++ jpegli at matched quality.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ projects: there is no C API, so you would write and maintain an extern "C" shim, and the code is AGPL-3.0-only unless you buy Imazen's commercial licence.

Throughput servers that already decode one image per core: single-thread baseline decode is 0.94x of libjpeg-turbo with the default upsampling, and the parallel speedups need restart markers that most camera and web JPEGs lack.

When output must be pixel-identical to libjpeg-turbo: the default IDCT differs and the default Triangle upsampling is only within max_diff 3; the pixel-exact Libjpeg IDCT is documented as adding about 37% overhead, which would put baseline decode well behind C (not measured in the README).

BGRA or RGBA output at large sizes until re-measured: the repo's BENCH-AUDIT.md found the streaming path emits RGB and then swizzles, measuring 4096x4096 single-thread Bgra 47% slower than Rgb and the imageflow BGRA bench 9 to 19% behind mozjpeg's JCS_EXT_BGRA (later sink-path work added a garb swizzle).
Code that needs a stable API: the crate is 0.x (0.9.0 in the repo while the README still says 0.8) and the README calls the decoder API prerelease with breaking changes expected.

integration.dependencies: Pure-Rust crates only (archmage, magetypes, garb, zenyuv, zenpixels, zencodec, zenanalyze, enough, memchr, aligned-vec, bytemuck, imgref, rgb, tinyvec, thiserror, whereat, linear-srgb); optional rayon (parallel), moxcms (color management), ultrahdr crates; no C dependencies
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.93 (MSRV, edition 2024); rust-toolchain.toml pins the stable channel only
integration.platforms: x86-64 (AVX2/FMA and AVX-512 by runtime dispatch, no target-cpu flags needed), aarch64 NEON, wasm32 SIMD128 (build with -C target-feature=+simd128), scalar fallback elsewhere; CI covers Linux, macOS and Windows on x86-64 and ARM64 plus i686
integration.thread_safety: Not documented beyond usage: the benches reuse one Decoder value across decode calls. With the parallel feature, decode runs on the global rayon pool by default (num_threads(0) = auto) whenever DRI is present and the image has 1024+ MCU blocks; num_threads(1) forces sequential.

gotchas: With --features parallel, a single decode() call fans out over every rayon thread when restart markers are present; in a server that already parallelizes across images set num_threads(1) to avoid oversubscription.

Open issue #215 (2026-10-02): decode_into() fails with 'internal error: coefficient data unavailable (streaming decode consumed entropy data)' on some baseline 4:2:0 JPEGs with restart markers (1024x768 with 11 RST, 2048x2048 photos with 31 RST), while decode() on the same bytes works.

The headline baseline numbers use non-pixel-exact defaults: the Jpegli integer IDCT plus Triangle upsampling within max_diff 3; the NearestNeighbor 1.03x figure uses a cheaper box upsample than libjpeg-turbo's fancy h2v2.

Bench-harness issues in zenjpeg/benches/decode_zenbench.rs, none of which change the README ratios: throughput is MiB/s of compressed JPEG input, not decoded pixels; the lane labelled 'zenjpeg LibjpegCompat (Libjpeg IDCT)' only sets Triangle upsampling (the default), so it re-runs the default config under a wrong label; and load_or_generate_pixels logs 'loaded' even when it falls back to synthetic pixels. CLAUDE.md attributes the 4096 parallel scaling to 'an 8-thread system' although the stated CPU is a 16-core Ryzen 9 7950X, so the thread count of the parallel table is unclear.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick zenjpeg over libjpeg-turbo-rs (pure-Rust libjpeg-turbo port claiming 0.77x to 0.93x of libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2's baseline decode time) when progressive decode, jpegli-class encoding, bounded-memory streaming or safety limits matter more than baseline libjpeg-compatible speed; pick jpeg-nitro (C) or plain libjpeg-turbo for C++ code, and mozjpeg-rs (same author) if you only need a mozjpeg-compatible encoder.
verified_claims_summary: First-party zenbench runs on a Ryzen 9 7950X under WSL2, cargo bench with the release profile (debug=true, no LTO, default target, runtime SIMD dispatch, rustc version unrecorded), against mozjpeg v4's libjpeg-turbo-derived decoder through mozjpeg-sys 2.2 with nasm_simd (C built by cc-rs at the Cargo profile's opt level with no -march; C compiler version unrecorded), read one scanline per call with default ISLOW IDCT and fancy upsampling, on 10 CID22 512x512 photos re-encoded by mozjpeg-rs at Q85 4:2:0: baseline 73.8 vs 78.1 MiB/s (0.94x) with defaults, 80.4 MiB/s with box upsampling, progressive 46 vs 34 MiB/s (1.35x); no committed result file or commit hash backs these CID22 figures. The 2.5x to 7.5x parallel figures (Feb 2026 synthetic set, commit 39f012f) compare multi-threaded zenjpeg with single-threaded libjpeg-turbo; single-threaded on the same set zenjpeg was only 1.05x to 1.07x faster.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-09-28, about 2,600 commits, 15 stars, 20 open issues, 7 open PRs) with frequent correctness fixes in 2026; usable as source only under AGPL-3.0 or with a paid (or $1 startup) commercial licence, and the decoder API is still prerelease.
